pricing.freeTierCaps: after the 7-day trial: existing data remains readable/exportable, but 0 new projects and 0 new invoices can be created

pricing.hiddenCosts: AI credits and workflow actions reset monthly. Extra credits, storage, and white-label options are paid add-ons whose live public prices were not disclosed.

verdictSummary: Do not mistake the interface for the product. Plutio's durable value is banking, compliance, trust, which a solo one-shot build cannot reproduce responsibly. The prompt therefore builds only the closest honest personal consolation tool.
coreLoopDIY: Build a private freelance work platform ledger that imports user-supplied CSV files, categorizes entries, reconciles balances, and exports reports.
diyTimeEstimate: not a true replacement; consolation build in one to two days
replacementScope: consolation build only; the paid product's moat remains
requirements: CSV exports from the user's own accounts
Explicit README warning that this is a consolation build, not a production replacement
whatYouLose: bank, payment, tax, and reconciliation integrations
live bank feeds and payment rails
whyPeopleStillPay: Plutio: People pay because errors touch real money. Bank connections, reconciliation, tax changes, evidence, security, and support are the product.
ongoingBurden: Own data integrity, backups, import mapping, reconciliation, security, audit logs, tax changes, and recovery.

notes: Credibility row: Plutio survives for a structural reason, not because its interface is difficult to copy.
prompt:
Build the closest honest consolation tool inspired by Plutio; do not claim to replace its structural moat.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a private freelance work platform ledger that imports user-supplied CSV files, categorizes entries, reconciles balances, and exports reports.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: multi-user controls and accountant workflows; bank, payment, tax, and reconciliation integrations; live bank feeds and payment rails.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
